name: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿAlī al-Rummānī
summary: Baghdad grammarian and Muʿtazilī theologian who explained Sībawayh with the tools of logic and wrote a book of definitions of grammar and a treatise on the inimitability of the Qurʾān.
bio: Al-Rummānī was born in Baghdad in 296/909 and learnt grammar with al-Zajjāj, Ibn al-Sarrāj and Ibn Durayd. He was a Muʿtazilī theologian as well as a grammarian, and he brought the definitions and divisions of the logicians into grammar more than any of his contemporaries.

His commentary on Sībawayh's al-Kitāb was famous for it, and so was the remark the biographers put in the mouth of Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī: 'If grammar is what al-Rummānī says, we have none of it; and if it is what we say, he has none of it.' His Kitāb al-Ḥudūd gathers the definitions of the terms of grammar, his Maʿānī al-ḥurūf treats the particles, and his al-Nukat fī iʿjāz al-Qurʾān is one of the first books on the eloquence of the Qurʾān. He died in Baghdad in 384/994.
uncertain: Al-Zubaydī's tenth Basran generation has an entry for 'ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā al-Baghdādhī al-Warrāq' (entry 51) whose text is lost; whether he is al-Rummānī is not certain.
